answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a non-transferable history of useful work: an identity earns larger rights only by completing verifiable tasks that independent peers, never its own invitees, attest over weeks, like a meadow that greens only where seeds were truly sown. A random audit lottery then echoes old claims back for re-checking, and any forged claim burns the identity's whole standing rather than one account. An operator mass-producing lotus copies would need months of genuine work per fake, so forgery costs more than honest participation, while a genuine newcomer starts small and grows.
